sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Detailed study guide and resources for Akbar Socio-Religious: The Final Phase - Din-i-Ilahi are currently being prepared. Check back soon for comprehensive explanations, summary diagrams, and expert preparation recommendations.

Key Dimensions of Study:

  • Definition, scope, and foundational theories.
  • Relevance to General Studies Paper & Contemporary contexts.
  • Core applications and structural framework.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the original name given by Akbar to the movement or code of spiritual conduct commonly known as Din-i-Ilahi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar originally called his system of spiritual path Tauhid-i-Ilahi, which translates to 'Divine Monotheism'. The term Din-i-Ilahi came into usage later. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year was the Ibadat Khana (House of Worship) constructed by Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri?
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar built the Ibadat Khana in 1575 at Fatehpur Sikri as a hall of prayer and religious discussions for scholars of various faiths. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following was the chief priest (Sadr) or the prominent ideologue assisting Akbar in drafting and formulating the Din-i-Ilahi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Abul Fazl was the chief ideologue and intellectual driving force behind Akbar's religious policies and Tauhid-i-Ilahi. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which prominent courtier of Akbar was the only Hindu to accept the Din-i-Ilahi?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to contemporary chroniclers like Badauni, Raja Birbal was the only Hindu notable who joined Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi. [Primary Reference: Badauni, Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the name of the decree or document issued in 1579 that gave Akbar the supreme authority to interpret religious laws in case of conflicting opinions among clergy?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Mahzar (Infallibility Decree) of 1579, drafted principally by Shaikh Mubarak, empowered Akbar to arbitrate religious disputes and take final decisions as the 'Sultan-i-Adil'. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: Who drafted the famous Mahzar of 1579?
practiceQuestions.sol: Shaikh Mubarak (father of Abul Fazl and Faizi) drafted the Mahzar, which was signed by leading ulema like Makhdum-ul-Mulk and Abdun Nabi. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which concept did Akbar promote to ensure absolute peace, tolerance, and harmony among all religious communities in his empire?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sulh-i-Kul means 'absolute peace' or 'peace with all'. It formed the cornerstone of Akbar's secular and pluralistic governance model. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did Akbar formally abolish the Jizya tax on non-Muslim subjects?
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar abolished Jizya in 1564, following his earlier abolition of the pilgrim tax (1563) and the practice of enslaving war captives (1562). [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary greeting formula used among the members of Din-i-Ilahi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Members of Din-i-Ilahi greeted each other with 'Allahu Akbar' and the response was 'Jalla Jalalahu' (May His glory be glorified). [Primary Reference: Abul Fazl, Akbarnama]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following contemporary historians was extremely critical of Akbar's religious policies and Din-i-Ilahi in his work 'Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Abdul Qadir Badauni was an orthodox Muslim scholar who vehemently criticized Akbar's deviation from orthodox Islam, portraying Din-i-Ilahi as a heresy in 'Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh'. [Primary Reference: Badauni, Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the debates held inside the Ibadat Khana contribute to the subsequent evolution of Akbar's religious outlook?
opts: They strengthened Akbar's faith in orthodox Sunni Islam exclusively.
The bitter sectarian quarrels disillusioned Akbar, leading him to realize that truth was not the monopoly of any single religion.
They resulted in the immediate conversion of the entire Mughal nobility to Christianity.
They led to the permanent abolition of the Mughal administrative machinery.
practiceQuestions.sol: Initially meant to uphold Sunni orthodoxy, the Ibadat Khana debates exposed bitter mutual recriminations among orthodox ulema. This deeply disillusioned Akbar and prompted him to seek universal truth through Sulh-i-Kul. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes the structural nature of Din-i-Ilahi?
opts: A rigid proselytizing institutional church with a holy scripture and mandatory dogmas.
An exclusive monastic order centered around personal devotion to the Emperor as the spiritual guide (Murshid).
A state-mandated political alliance exclusively between Rajputs and Mughals.
A fiscal code designed to regulate agricultural taxation across imperial provinces.
practiceQuestions.sol: Din-i-Ilahi was not a new religion with a holy book, clergy, or places of worship. Rather, it was a select group of imperial courtiers bound by discipleship (Muridi) to Akbar, who acted as their spiritual guide. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the political implication of Akbar issuing the Mahzar of 1579?
opts: It subordinated royal authority to the supreme dictates of the Ottoman Caliph.
It centralized supreme religious-legal arbitration power in the hands of the Emperor, freeing him from dependency on the orthodox ulema.
It declared Islam as the exclusive state religion while banning all other faiths.
It dissolved the Mughal Mansabdari system entirely.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Mahzar bypassed the monopoly of the orthodox ulema (clergy) over religious interpretations, vesting ultimate legal-religious authority in Akbar if opinions among scholars conflicted. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Akbar’s policy of 'Sulh-i-Kul' reflect in his administrative and judicial appointments?
opts: High administrative and military offices were opened to capable individuals regardless of their religious affiliation, including Rajputs, Iranians, and Turanis.
Only Sunni Muslims were allowed to hold Mansabs above 1000.
Judicial posts were reserved exclusively for orthodox Qazis trained in Medina.
Hindus were barred from holding revenue administration posts.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sulh-i-Kul was translated into practice by broad-basing the nobility. Akbar inducted Rajputs, Shias, Iranians, and Turanis into the Mansabdari system, prioritizing loyalty and competence over religious identity. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: Modern historians view Akbar's religious experiments primarily as:
opts: A cynical political maneuver to destroy Islam completely.
A sincere pursuit of universal harmony and an instrument of state integration in a pluralistic society.
An attempt to establish a Portuguese-backed Christian empire in India.
A temporary strategy to collect more taxes from temple properties.
practiceQuestions.sol: Historians emphasize that Akbar's socio-religious policies were driven by a genuine quest for truth and a pragmatic need to forge a cohesive ruling elite across diverse ethnic and religious groups. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What role did translations of Sanskrit texts into Persian (at the Maktab Khana) play in Akbar's socio-religious policy?
opts: They were done solely to destroy Hindu philosophical texts.
They bridged cultural gaps, fostered mutual understanding, and reduced intellectual barriers between diverse religious communities.
They were intended to replace Arabic as the administrative language of the empire.
They served as tax registers for agrarian assessments.
practiceQuestions.sol: By establishing the Maktab Khana (translation bureau), Akbar commissioned Persian translations of works like the Mahabharata (Razm-nama), Ramayana, and Upanishads, promoting inter-religious synthesis and mutual respect. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did orthodox Islamic elements react so strongly against Akbar's socio-religious measures?
opts: Because Akbar imposed compulsory conversion of Muslims to Hinduism.
Because Akbar challenged the monopoly of the ulema, questioned orthodox tenets, and placed all religions on an equal footing.
Because Akbar abolished the Persian script entirely.
Because Akbar banned the practice of congregational Friday prayers.
practiceQuestions.sol: Orthodox ulema felt threatened as Akbar curtailed their judicial privileges, undermined their exclusive authority via the Mahzar, and questioned injunctions like cow slaughter and purdah. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Akbar reform social customs regarding child marriage and sati?
opts: He instituted total capital punishment for anyone attending a child marriage.
He discouraged child marriage by fixing minimum age limits and regulated sati by requiring official permission to prevent forced immolation.
He completely ignored social evils, focusing exclusively on military expansion.
He made sati mandatory for widows of high-ranking nobles.
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar attempted progressive social reforms: discouraging child marriages, allowing widow remarriage, and checking forcible sati by insisting that a widow's consent be verified by state officials. [Primary Reference: Abul Fazl, Ain-i-Akbari]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the 'Surya Namaskar' and reverence of light (Ayn) introduced in Akbar's court?
opts: They were pagan rituals designed to worship Greek mythological gods.
They reflected the synthesis of Persian solar symbolism (farr-i-izadi) and Indian traditions, portraying the king as a divine light.
They were military drills practiced by the imperial artillery corps.
They were agricultural ceremonies conducted before sowing wheat.
practiceQuestions.sol: Akbar incorporated light symbolism—drawing from Zoroastrian sun veneration and Hindu concepts—to project the concept of 'Farr-i-Izadi' (divine light emanating from the sovereign), cementing royal absolutism. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Akbar's religious policies impact the long-term stability of the Mughal Empire?
opts: They created permanent political instability and continuous civil wars.
They fostered broad-based indigenous support and loyalty, mitigating religious polarization and securing imperial consolidation.
They completely bankrupted the imperial treasury within two years.
They forced the migration of all artisans to neighboring Safavid Persia.
practiceQuestions.sol: By integrating diverse religious and ethnic groups through Sulh-i-Kul, Akbar laid a resilient sociopolitical foundation that sustained the Mughal Empire through decades of expansion and prosperity. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Din-i-Ilahi:
1. It was a formal proselytizing religion established by Akbar with its own sacred scripture and mandatory places of worship.
2. Membership of Din-i-Ilahi was restricted exclusively to high-ranking imperial officers and close personal favorites of the Emperor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Din-i-Ilahi had no sacred scripture, no priesthood, no dogmas, and no places of worship. Statement 2 is correct as it was an exclusive order of disciples (Murids) drawn from trusted courtiers and nobles around Akbar. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri:
1. It was initially constructed exclusively for religious discussions among Sunni theologians.
2. Later, Akbar opened its doors to theologians of all religions, including Christians, Zoroastrians, Hindus, and Jains.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Ibadat Khana (built in 1575) initially hosted only Sunni ulema. However, due to bitter sectarian squabbles among them, Akbar opened discussions to Shias, Sufis, Hindus, Jains, Parsis, and Christians (Jesuit priests). [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mahzar of 1579:
1. It was drafted by Abul Fazl.
2. It declared the Emperor as the final arbiter (Sultan-i-Adil) in religious disputes when ulema held conflicting opinions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Mahzar was drafted by Shaikh Mubarak (Abul Fazl's father), not Abul Fazl himself. Statement 2 is correct as it empowered Akbar as the supreme interpreter of religious law (Sultan-i-Adil). [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's concept of 'Sulh-i-Kul':
1. It formed the ethical and administrative foundation of the Mughal state under Akbar.
2. It advocated religious intolerance towards minority communities to maintain state cohesion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Sulh-i-Kul ('absolute peace') was the core principle of Akbar's governance. Statement 2 is incorrect because Sulh-i-Kul specifically meant universal tolerance and peace among all religions, rejecting religious intolerance. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Akbar's social legislation:
1. Akbar abolished the pilgrim tax in 1563 and the Jizya tax in 1564.
2. He legalized child marriage and encouraged compulsory conversions during wartime.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is entirely incorrect; Akbar discouraged child marriage by raising marriageable ages, prohibited forced conversions, and abolished the enslavement of war captives in 1562. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Jesuit missions at Akbar's court:
1. Akbar invited Jesuit priests from Goa to participate in theological debates at his court.
2. The Jesuits successfully converted Akbar to Roman Catholicism before his death.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; three Jesuit missions visited Fatehpur Sikri upon Akbar's invitation. Statement 2 is incorrect because despite their deep engagement, the Jesuits failed to convert Akbar, who maintained an eclectic spiritual stance. [Primary Reference: Smith, Akbar the Great Mogul]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of Abul Fazl in formulating Akbar's ideology:
1. Abul Fazl authored the 'Akbarnama' and 'Ain-i-Akbari', which provided ideological justification for Akbar's absolute monarchy and Sulh-i-Kul.
2. He was a staunch supporter of orthodox Sunni clerical dominance in state affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect; Abul Fazl strongly opposed orthodox clerical dominance and was the principal intellectual architect of Akbar's liberal, pluralistic imperial ideology. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History Part II]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about cultural and religious synthesis under Akbar:
1. Akbar established the Maktab Khana for translating Sanskrit classics into Persian to bridge cultural divides.
2. Painting studios patronized by Akbar exclusively illustrated orthodox Islamic theological manuscripts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because imperial ateliers illustrated a vast array of texts, including Persian translations of Hindu epics like Mahabharata and Ramayana, blending Persian, Indian, and European artistic styles rather than confining themselves to orthodox Islamic texts. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the opposition faced by Akbar's religious policies:
1. Mirza Hakim, Akbar's half-brother in Kabul, was instigated by orthodox elements in India to launch an invasion against Akbar.
2. The rebellion in Bengal and Bihar (1580-1581) was partly fueled by religious grievances against the Mahzar and Akbar's religious liberalism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Disgruntled orthodox elements, led by religious figures in the eastern provinces and coordinated with discontented nobles, issued fatwas against Akbar and encouraged Mirza Hakim's invasion. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the historical assessment of Din-i-Ilahi by contemporary and modern scholars:
1. Badauni viewed Din-i-Ilahi as an apostasy and accused Akbar of turning away from Islam.
2. Modern academic consensus views Din-i-Ilahi as a successful mass religious movement that converted a majority of the Mughal populace.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Badauni severely castigated Akbar for heresy in Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh. Statement 2 is incorrect because Din-i-Ilahi never became a mass movement and remained confined to a handful of imperial courtiers, dying out almost entirely after Akbar's death. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]
